content.value_statement: Agent tools often fail because schemas, errors, and validation are unclear. This skill gives practical patterns for tool schemas, MCP servers, runners, and parallel calls.
actual_capabilities: Explains JSON Schema patterns for tool names, parameters, enums, and required fields.
Shows how to add input examples that guide Claude tool use.
Covers error response structures that help agents recover from failures.
Provides MCP server patterns for listing and calling tools.
Describes Anthropic tool runner usage in Python and TypeScript.
Outlines parallel tool execution patterns and validation checks.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not generate a complete production service.
Examples need adaptation for each provider, runtime, and security model.
It does not replace integration tests or expert review.
It does not include runnable project files beyond documentation examples.

use_cases.title: Design Function Tools
use_cases.description: Create schemas and error behavior for APIs that agents can call reliably.

use_cases.title: Improve Tool Calling Accuracy
use_cases.description: Use examples, enums, and descriptions to reduce invalid tool inputs.

use_cases.title: Plan MCP Tool Servers
use_cases.description: Map reusable tools to MCP list and call handlers.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Tool Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design one agent tool for this task: [task]. Include the tool name, purpose, required inputs, optional inputs, and return format.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Tool Description
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review this tool description: [description]. Make it clearer about when to use the tool, parameters, limits, and output.

prompt_templates.title: Design Error Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define validation errors, external service errors, business errors, and recovery messages for this tool: [tool summary].

prompt_templates.title: Plan an MCP Tool Suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan an MCP server for [domain]. Define tool boundaries, schemas, call handling, permissions, and parallel execution rules.

output_examples.input: I need a weather tool for an agent.
output: A suggested tool name, parameters, and return format.
Validation rules for location and unit inputs.
Clear error cases for unknown locations, timeouts, and rate limits.

output_examples.input: Review my tool set for parallel use.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify independent tools, suggest parallel invocation rules, and warn where ordering or shared state requires sequential execution.

output_examples.input: Help me design an MCP server for customer records.
output: A list of safe tool boundaries.
Error handling expectations for missing records and permission failures.

best_practices: Write tool descriptions that explain when to use the tool and when not to use it.
Validate all agent-provided inputs before a tool calls external systems.
Return concise string results with clear error messages and recovery hints.
anti_patterns: Do not create many overlapping tools with similar names or scopes.
Do not hide tool failures behind empty or generic error responses.
Do not accept free-form input when enums or structured fields are possible.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design AI agent tools with schemas, validation, error handling, MCP patterns, and execution guidance.

faq.question: Does it create production code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and examples that developers must adapt and test.

faq.question: Which platforms does it mention?
faq.answer: It covers Claude, OpenAI function calling, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain tools, and MCP.

faq.question: Can it improve Claude Code or Codex workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps structure tools that Claude Code and Codex can reason about clearly.

faq.question: Does it address security?
faq.answer: It emphasizes input validation, permission errors, timeouts, and parameterized SQL for safer tool behavior.

faq.question: When should I use another skill?
faq.answer: Use another skill for multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory, voice agents, computer control, or evaluation details.
